name: Acne Scars
summary: Acne scars are a change in the skin's structure, not its colour, and the type of scar decides what is likely to help.
leadAnswer: Acne scarring is a change in the skin's structure, felt as a dip or an irregularity once inflammation has settled. Scars do not fade on their own; they are remodelled gradually, over months. Pico laser is mainly for flat marks rather than texture, so depressed scars usually start with RF microneedling or a resurfacing laser.

facts.label: A scar is a change in the skin's structure you can feel, not only a mark you can see.
Ice pick, boxcar, rolling and raised scars respond to different approaches.
Scar treatment usually starts once active breakouts are under control.

sections.heading: What are acne scars?
body: A scar is a change in the skin's structure, felt as a dip or a raised area. A mark is flat: red or brown discolouration on smooth skin.

drivers.heading: What makes acne more likely to scar
drivers.intro: Scarring follows inflammation. What raises the chance of it:

items.body: deep, firm, painful lumps under the skin that do not come to a head carry the highest risk of permanent scarring.
the longer deep, inflamed acne goes on, the more chance it leaves permanent change.
cheeks mark and scar readily, and lesions on the back, chest and shoulders are more likely to leave raised rather than depressed scars.

variant.heading: Which kind of scar do I have?
variant.intro: Most people have more than one type.

tabs.label: Depressed
tabs.title: Depressed scars

items.body: wider depressions with defined edges, like a shallow crater.
soft, wave-like undulations caused by tethering beneath the skin.

tabs.routing: RF microneedling or resurfacing laser, often over several sessions, with combinations chosen by scar type.

tabs.label: Raised
tabs.title: Raised scars (hypertrophic or keloid)
tabs.body: Firm, thickened tissue sitting above skin level. More common on the chest, shoulders and back.
tabs.routing: a separate assessment, because the approach differs from depressed scarring.

tabs.label: Marks
tabs.title: Marks, not scars
tabs.body: Flat red or brown discolouration on smooth skin. Not a scar, and often fades on its own over months.

items.body: (post-inflammatory erythema), from dilated blood vessels near the surface. More visible on lighter skin.
(post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation), from excess pigment produced during inflammation. Very common in the medium and deeper skin tones seen across Malaysia, and worsened by sun exposure.

treatmentsIntro: Which treatment fits depends on scar type, skin tone and how much recovery time you can plan around.

microneedling.why: For rolling and boxcar scars, including on deeper skin tones
microneedling.body: Fine needles deliver radiofrequency energy into the deeper layer of the skin to stimulate collagen.

resurfacing-laser.why: For established scarring, where the recovery time works for you
resurfacing-laser.body: A fractional CO₂ laser used where scarring is more established.

pico-laser.why: For the flat marks around scars, rather than the dips themselves
pico-laser.body: A picosecond laser that targets pigment in short, high-speed pulses.

exosome-therapy.why: To support the skin after scar treatment, as an adjunct
exosome-therapy.body: A regenerative approach applied after energy-based treatment to support skin recovery. The evidence base is still developing.

items.body: Redness, swelling, dryness, flaking and a warm or gritty sensation for a few days. Less common effects include prolonged redness, blistering, infection, or a change in skin pigment.

Medium and deeper skin tones, common across Malaysia, carry a higher chance of post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation after energy-based treatment. This is why doctors here often choose gentler settings and longer intervals between sessions.
Daily broad-spectrum sunscreen is part of the plan for every treatment listed above, both before and after.
Scars are improved, rarely erased, and ice pick scars rarely resolve with energy devices alone. Treating scars does not stop new breakouts. Collagen remodels over months.

risks.disclose: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, take or recently took oral acne medication, have a history of cold sores, keloid scarring or recent tanning, or have had any skin procedure in the past few weeks. Any of these may change what is appropriate or when.

faqs.q: Can acne scars be removed completely?
faqs.a: Depressed scarring can often be improved, though rarely erased. Treatments like RF microneedling and resurfacing lasers work by stimulating the skin to remodel its own collagen, which takes place gradually over months rather than immediately.

faqs.q: Is pico laser used for acne scars?
faqs.a: Pico laser is most relevant to the flat marks and discolouration acne leaves, rather than to the texture of a scar. Some pico devices carry a fractional lens array that the manufacturer indicates for acne scars in skin types I to IV.

faqs.q: Can ice pick scars be treated?
faqs.a: Ice pick scars are narrow, deep pits and the hardest type to treat with energy devices alone; they rarely resolve fully that way. Rolling and boxcar scars usually respond better.

faqs.q: Can I treat my scars while I still have active acne?
faqs.a: Usually not yet. Treating scarring while acne is still active usually does not work well, and treating active acne will not remove existing scars.

faqs.q: Is laser treatment for acne scars safe on Asian skin?
faqs.a: Yes, when the device and settings are chosen appropriately by a doctor who is experienced with your skin type. The specific concern with medium and deeper skin tones is post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation, the skin responding to treatment by producing extra pigment. It's a real consideration, not a reason to avoid treatment.

faqs.q: What is the downtime after acne scar treatment?
faqs.a: After RF microneedling, most people wait until the redness settles, typically two to three days. After fractional CO2 resurfacing, expect redness, swelling and a hot, tight feeling for the first day or two, then several days of bronzing and flaking; a lighter session commonly settles within about a week, and deeper settings take longer.

Most people describe energy-based treatments as uncomfortable rather than painful. Topical numbing cream is applied beforehand where appropriate, and cooling is used during and after. Ablative resurfacing is more uncomfortable than non-ablative treatments, and RF microneedling is generally felt more than pico laser.

faqs.q: Can acne scars on the back or chest be treated?
faqs.a: Yes, though these areas behave differently from the face. Skin on the back and chest is thicker, lesions there tend to be larger, and scarring is more likely to be raised than depressed, which calls for a different approach entirely.
